at savne.explanation: "At savne" means "to miss" someone or something that is not here: Jeg savner min familie (I miss my family). For missing a bus, Danes say Jeg nåede ikke bussen (I did not catch the bus).

sentence.en: I will miss my family a lot.

at se.explanation: "At se" means "to see", and also "to watch": Jeg ser en film (I am watching a film). Jeg kan se, hvad du mener means "I can see what you mean". Vi ses! means "See you!". At kigge (to look) is on purpose: Kig her! (Look here!).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **se** dit hus fra her.
sentence.en: I can see your house from here.

at se på.explanation: "At se på" means "to look at": Jeg ser på billedet (I am looking at the picture). Do not mix it up with at se (to see) or at lede efter (to look for): Jeg leder efter min nøgle (I am looking for my key).

sentence.en: I want to look at the picture.

at se tv.explanation: "At se tv" means "to watch TV". Danish uses se (to see) where English says "watch", as in se en film (to watch a film). At se fjernsyn (to watch television) means the same. Tv is said as two letters, te-ve.

sentence.en: We want to watch TV tonight.

at sende.explanation: "At sende" means "to send", for example a letter, a parcel or an email. The person who gets it comes right after sender (send), with no word for "to": Jeg sender dig en besked (I send you a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to send a letter to Mum.

at sende en sms.explanation: "At sende en sms" means "to text", or literally to send an SMS. To say who gets it, put them after sende (send): Jeg sender dig en sms (I send you a text).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **sende en sms** til min ven.
sentence.en: I want to send a text to my friend.

at servere.explanation: "At servere" means "to serve" food or drinks, for example in a restaurant or for guests at home. Maden bliver serveret klokken 18 means "The food is served at 6 pm".

sentence.en: The waiter will serve the food now.

at sidde.explanation: "At sidde" means "to sit": Jeg sidder på en stol (I am sitting on a chair). Jeg sidder ved computeren means "I am sitting at the computer". To sit down is at sætte sig (literally to put oneself).

sentence.en: You can sit on the chair.

at sige.explanation: "At sige" means "to say": Hvad siger du? (What are you saying?). At sige hej means "to say hi". To tell a story, use at fortælle (to tell) instead.

sentence.en: The children must say thank you.

at sige farvel.explanation: "At sige farvel" means "to say goodbye". Farvel (goodbye) can sound a little final. Among friends, Danes more often say hej hej (bye bye) or vi ses (see you).

sentence.da: Vi skal **sige farvel** til vores gæster.
sentence.en: We have to say goodbye to our guests.

at sige goddag.explanation: "At sige goddag" means "to say hello", literally to say good day. Goddag is a rather formal or old-fashioned greeting. With friends you would normally say hej (hi).

sentence.da: Du skal **sige goddag** til min mor.
sentence.en: You must say hello to my mother.

at skifte tøj.explanation: "At skifte tøj" means "to change clothes". At skifte on its own means "to change" or "to switch" something, such as skifte job (to change jobs).

sentence.da: Jeg er våd og vil **skifte tøj**.
sentence.en: I am wet and want to change clothes.

at skrive.explanation: "At skrive" means "to write": Jeg skriver et brev (I am writing a letter). It also covers typing and texting: skrive en besked (to write a message).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **skrive** et brev til mor.
sentence.en: I want to write a letter to Mum.

at skulle.explanation: "At skulle" means "to have to" or "should": Jeg skal arbejde (I have to work). It is also used for plans: Jeg skal i skole (I am going to school).

sentence.da: Jeg vil ikke **skulle** arbejde i morgen.
sentence.en: I don't want to have to work tomorrow.

at slappe af.explanation: "At slappe af" means "to relax" or "to take it easy". Slap af! means "Relax!" or "Calm down!".

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og vil **slappe af**.
sentence.en: I am tired and want to relax.

at slukke.explanation: "At slukke" means "to turn off" a light or "to put out" a fire: slukke lyset (turn off the light) and slukke en brand (put out a fire). For a TV or the radio, use slukke for (turn off): slukke for fjernsynet (turn off the TV).

sentence.en: Remember to turn off the light.

at slukke for.explanation: "At slukke for" means "to turn off" something like the TV, the radio or the heating: Jeg slukker for radioen (I turn off the radio). For a light, slukke lyset (turn off the light) is the usual choice. A fire is put out with plain slukke: slukke en brand (to put out a fire).

sentence.en: Remember to turn off the TV.

at slutte.explanation: "At slutte" means "to end" or "to finish": Skolen slutter klokken tre (School ends at three). With med (with) it means "to stop doing something": Jeg slutter med at ryge (I am quitting smoking).

sentence.en: School is going to end at three.

at smage.explanation: "At smage" means "to taste", both trying food and having a flavor. Det smager godt means "It tastes good" and "Det smager af citron" means "It tastes of lemon".

sentence.en: I want to taste the good cake.

at smile.explanation: "At smile" means "to smile". Hun smilede til mig means "She smiled at me": you smile til (to) someone.

sentence.da: Hun er glad og kan **smile** til alle.
sentence.en: She is happy and can smile at everyone.

at snakke.explanation: "At snakke" means "to talk" or "to chat", and it is the everyday word for speaking. Kan vi snakke sammen? means "Can we talk?". At tale (to speak) is a bit more formal.

sentence.da: Jeg har tid og kan **snakke** nu.
sentence.en: I have time and can talk now.

at snakke om.explanation: "At snakke om" means "to talk about": Vi snakker om mad (We are talking about food). To talk with a person, use med (with): Jeg snakker med min mor (I talk with my mother).

sentence.da: Vi vil **snakke om** vores ferie i aften.
sentence.en: We want to talk about our holiday tonight.

at sne.explanation: "At sne" means "to snow": Det sner (It is snowing). The word for snow itself is also "sne", as in Der er sne (There is snow), so the sentence shows which one is meant.

sentence.en: In winter it can snow a lot.

at sove.explanation: "At sove" means "to sleep": Jeg sover godt (I sleep well). Going to bed is a different phrase: at gå i seng (to go to bed). Sov godt means "Sleep well".

sentence.en: The children are tired and want to sleep.

at spille.explanation: "At spille" means "to play" a game, a sport or an instrument: Jeg spiller guitar (I play the guitar) and Vi spiller fodbold (We play football). It also means "to act" a part. For children playing for fun, Danes say at lege (to play).

sentence.da: Min bror kan **spille** guitar og synge.
sentence.en: My brother can play the guitar and sing.

at spille fodbold.explanation: "At spille fodbold" means "to play soccer" ("football" in Britain). Spille (to play) is used for most games and sports. The word fodbold is built from fod (foot) and bold (ball), and there is no en (a) before it.

sentence.en: The children want to play soccer today.

at spise.explanation: "At spise" means "to eat": Vi spiser aftensmad (We eat dinner). At spise ude means "to eat out". For drinking, use at drikke (to drink).

sentence.en: We want to eat dinner now.

at spørge.explanation: "At spørge" means "to ask" a question: Jeg spørger ham om vejen (I ask him for directions). To ask for something you want, use at bede om (to ask for): Jeg beder om en kop kaffe (I ask for a cup of coffee).

sentence.en: I want to ask the teacher.

at spørge om.explanation: "At spørge om" means "to ask about" or "to ask for": spørge om prisen (ask about the price) and spørge om vej (ask for directions). Må jeg spørge dig om noget? means "May I ask you something?".

sentence.en: I want to ask for help.

at spørge om vej.explanation: "At spørge om vej" means "to ask for directions", literally to ask about way: Undskyld, må jeg spørge om vej? (Excuse me, may I ask for directions?).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **spørge om vej** til banegården.
sentence.en: I want to ask for directions to the station.

at starte.explanation: "At starte" means "to start", for people and for machines: Bilen starter ikke (The car won't start) and Vi starter i morgen (We start tomorrow). At begynde (to begin) means almost the same.

sentence.en: The film is going to start at eight.

at stave.explanation: "At stave" means "to spell": Kan du stave det? means "Can you spell that?".

sentence.en: Can you spell your name?

at stille uret.explanation: "At stille uret" means "to set the clock". You can say which way: stille uret en time frem (set the clock an hour forward) or stille uret en time tilbage (set the clock an hour back).

sentence.da: Vi skal **stille uret** en time tilbage.
sentence.en: We have to set the clock back an hour.

at stoppe.explanation: "At stoppe" means "to stop": Bussen stopper her (The bus stops here). With med (with) it means "to quit doing something": Jeg stopper med at spise slik (I am quitting eating sweets).

sentence.en: The bus will stop here.

at studere.explanation: "At studere" means "to study", especially at a university: Jeg studerer historie (I study history). For studying at home for a test, Danes often say at læse til en eksamen (literally to read for an exam).

related.en: a study, a course of study

sentence.en: She wants to study medicine at the university.

at stå.explanation: "At stå" means "to stand", but Danish uses it more widely than English: Flasken står på bordet means "The bottle is on the table", and "Der står noget på skiltet" means "Something is written on the sign".

sentence.en: I want to stand by the window.

at stå i kø.explanation: "At stå i kø" means to stand in line (or "to queue"), literally to stand in queue: Jeg står i kø i supermarkedet (I am standing in line at the supermarket).

sentence.da: Vi må **stå i kø** for billetter.
sentence.en: We have to stand in line for tickets.

at stå op.explanation: "At stå op" means "to get up" out of bed, literally to stand up. In the I have form Danish uses er (am) instead of har (have): Jeg er stået op (I have gotten up). To stand up from a chair, Danes say at rejse sig (to stand up).

sentence.en: I want to get up at seven.

at stå på ski.explanation: "At stå på ski" means "to ski", literally to stand on skis. Water skiing works the same way: at stå på vandski (to water ski). There is no en or et (a) before ski.

sentence.da: Vi vil **stå på ski** i Norge.
sentence.en: We want to ski in Norway.

at svare.explanation: "At svare" means "to answer" or "to reply". To answer a question, add på (on): svare på et spørgsmål (to answer a question).

sentence.en: I can answer the question.

at svømme.explanation: "At svømme" means "to swim": Jeg svømmer i havet (I swim in the sea). For a quick dip, Danes also say at bade (to go for a swim): Vi bader i søen (We are going for a swim in the lake).

sentence.en: Fish can swim in the water.

at synes.explanation: "At synes" means "to think", in the sense of having an opinion: Jeg synes, det er godt (I think it is good). For a guess about a fact, use at tro (to believe, to guess): Jeg tror, han kommer (I think he is coming). Hvad synes du? means "What do you think?".

sentence.en: What do you think about the food?

at synge.explanation: "At synge" means "to sing". To sing along with others or with a recording, add med (with): Jeg synger med (I sing along).

sentence.en: She can sing a beautiful song.

at sælge.explanation: "At sælge" means "to sell". Til salg means "for sale", as on a sign: Bilen er til salg (The car is for sale).

sentence.da: Han vil **sælge** sin bil for penge.
sentence.en: He wants to sell his car for money.

at sætte.explanation: "At sætte" means "to put" or "to place" something somewhere: Jeg sætter bogen på hylden (I put the book on the shelf). Do not mix it up with at sidde (to sit), which describes where you already are. Sæt dig means "Sit down".

sentence.en: I want to put the cup on the table.

at sætte sig.explanation: "At sætte sig" means "to sit down": Jeg sætter mig i sofaen (I sit down on the sofa). To say you are already sitting, use at sidde (to sit): Jeg sidder i sofaen (I am sitting on the sofa).

sentence.en: He wants to sit down on the chair.

en salat.explanation: "En salat" means "a salad" and also "lettuce", so the situation tells you which one is meant. En grøn salat means "a green salad".

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **salat** med tomat og agurk.
sentence.en: I eat a salad with tomato and cucumber.

en sandal.explanation: "En sandal" means "a sandal". Sandals come in pairs, so you will often see et par sandaler (a pair of sandals).

sentence.da: Jeg har en **sandal** på hver fod.
sentence.en: I have a sandal on each foot.

en sandwich.explanation: "En sandwich" means "a sandwich", bread with a filling, closed on top. Smørrebrød (open sandwich) has no top slice of bread.

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **sandwich** med ost og skinke.
sentence.en: I eat a sandwich with cheese and ham.

en seng.explanation: "En seng" means "a bed". At gå i seng means "to go to bed", with no en in it: Jeg går i seng (I am going to bed).

sentence.da: Jeg er træt og går i **seng**.
sentence.en: I am tired and go to bed.

en serviet.explanation: "En serviet" means "a napkin", the cloth or paper you use at the table while eating. It is said ser-vi-ET, with the stress at the end.

sentence.en: There is a napkin by the fork.

en side.explanation: "En side" means "a page" or "a side", and also a web page. På side ti means "on page ten" and "på den anden side" means "on the other side". På den ene side ... på den anden side means "on the one hand ... on the other hand".

sentence.en: Open the book on page ten.

en skadestue.explanation: "En skadestue" means an ER (emergency room), where you go for injuries and sudden problems. It is made of skade (injury) and stue (room). Jeg er på skadestuen means "I am at the ER", literally on the ER.

sentence.da: Der er en **skadestue** på sygehuset i byen.
sentence.en: There is an ER at the hospital in the city.

en ske.explanation: "En ske" means "a spoon". En teske (a teaspoon) and en spiseske (a tablespoon, literally an eating spoon) are built from it.

sentence.en: I eat the soup with a spoon.

en skinke.explanation: "En skinke" means "a ham". For ham on bread or in a meal, just skinke is used, for example et stykke skinke (a piece of ham) and brød med skinke (bread with ham).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have brød med **skinke** og ost.
sentence.en: I want bread with ham and cheese.

en skive.explanation: "En skive" means "a slice", for example of bread, cheese or sausage: en skive brød (a slice of bread) and to skiver ost (two slices of cheese). For a slice of cake Danes usually say et stykke kage (a piece of cake).

sentence.en: I want a slice of bread.

en skjorte.explanation: "En skjorte" means "a shirt". The j in skjorte is said like an English y.

sentence.en: He is wearing a white shirt.

en sko.explanation: "En sko" means "a shoe". The word for more than one shoe looks the same as the single word, so you tell them apart with a number: to sko means "two shoes".

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **sko** på min fod.
sentence.en: I put a shoe on my foot.

en skobutik.explanation: "En skobutik" means "a shoe store". It is made of sko (shoes) and butik (shop).

sentence.da: Jeg køber nye sko i en **skobutik**.
sentence.en: I buy new shoes in a shoe store.

en skole.explanation: "En skole" means "a school". To say that someone is at school, Danes say i skole with no en or "the": Børnene er i skole (The children are at school).

sentence.da: Min datter går i **skole** hver dag.
sentence.en: My daughter goes to school every day.

en skov.explanation: "En skov" means "a forest" or "woods". A walk in the woods is en skovtur (literally a forest trip).

sentence.da: Der er mange høje træer i en **skov**.
sentence.en: There are many tall trees in a forest.

en skulder.explanation: "En skulder" means "a shoulder". Danish says the shoulder where English says my shoulder: Jeg har ondt i skulderen (literally I have pain in the shoulder) means "My shoulder hurts". At trække på skuldrene means "to shrug".

sentence.da: Hun lægger sin arm om min **skulder**.
sentence.en: She puts her arm around my shoulder.

en sky.explanation: "En sky" means "a cloud". There is also a different word sky that means "shy": Han er sky (He is shy). The sentence tells you which one is meant.

sentence.da: Der er en mørk **sky** på himlen.
sentence.en: There is a dark cloud in the sky.

en skål.explanation: "En skål" means "a bowl". The same word, Skål!, is what you say when you raise a glass, like Cheers!.

sentence.en: I eat soup from a bowl.

en smartphone.explanation: "En smartphone" means "a smartphone". En mobil (a mobile phone) is the shorter everyday word and can mean any mobile phone.

sentence.da: Jeg bruger min **smartphone** til at ringe.
sentence.en: I use my smartphone to call.

en smerte.explanation: "En smerte" means "a pain". It is mostly used in the plural: Jeg har smerter means "I am in pain". For a pain in one place Danes often say ondt, as in Jeg har ondt i hovedet (literally I have pain in the head, meaning "my head hurts").

sentence.da: Jeg har en skarp **smerte** i foden.
sentence.en: I have a sharp pain in my foot.

en sms.explanation: "En sms" means "a text message", said es-em-es. Jeg sender dig en sms (I am sending you a text). For messages in chat apps Danes usually say en besked (a message).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en kort **sms** til dig.
sentence.en: I write a short text message to you.

en snack.explanation: "En snack" means "a snack". Another way to say it is en bid mad (a bite of food).

sentence.en: I eat a snack before dinner.

en sodavand.explanation: "En sodavand" means "a soda", a fizzy soft drink such as cola or lemonade. It is built from soda (soda water) and vand (water).

sentence.da: Jeg drikker en kold **sodavand** i dag.
sentence.en: I drink a cold soda today.

en sofa.explanation: "En sofa" means "a sofa" or "a couch". The low table in front of it is et sofabord (a coffee table), built from sofa and bord (table).

sentence.en: We sit on a soft sofa.

en sok.explanation: "En sok" means "a sock". Et par sokker means "a pair of socks", and "Jeg mangler en sok" means "I am missing a sock".

sentence.da: Jeg har en **sok** på min venstre fod.
sentence.en: I have a sock on my left foot.

en sol.explanation: "En sol" means "a sun", but you mostly hear it as solen (the sun): Solen skinner means "The sun is shining". It is also part of solskin (sunshine) and solbriller (sunglasses).

sentence.da: Der er meget **sol** og varmt i dag.
sentence.en: There is a lot of sun and it is warm today.

en sommer.explanation: "En sommer" means "a summer". You say i sommer (this summer) and næste sommer (next summer).

sentence.en: This summer we swim in the sea.

en sommerferie.explanation: "En sommerferie" means "a summer vacation". It is built from sommer (summer) and ferie (holiday), and you say i sommerferien (during the summer vacation).

sentence.da: I vores **sommerferie** bader vi i havet.
sentence.en: In our summer vacation we swim in the sea.

en sovs.explanation: "En sovs" means "a sauce" or "gravy". Tomatsovs (tomato sauce) is built on it. The spelling en sauce (a sauce) is also used.

sentence.en: The meatballs taste good with brown gravy.

en spisning.explanation: "En spisning" means "a shared meal", an event that people organise together, for example for a club. For an ordinary meal, say et måltid (a meal).

sentence.da: Vi laver mad sammen til klubbens **spisning**.
sentence.en: We cook together for the club's shared meal.

en station.explanation: "En station" means "a station", a place where trains, metros or buses stop. På stationen means "at the station". For a train station only, say en togstation (a train station).

sentence.da: Vi venter på toget på en **station**.
sentence.en: We wait for the train at a station.

en stegepande.explanation: "En stegepande" means "a frying pan". It is stege (to fry) and pande (pan) joined into one word. You can also say just en pande (a pan).

sentence.da: Jeg steger æg på en varm **stegepande**.
sentence.en: I fry eggs in a hot frying pan.

en sten.explanation: "En sten" means "a stone" or "a rock". The plural sten looks the same as the singular, so mange sten means "many stones". As a material, sten is used alone: et hus af sten (a house of stone).

sentence.en: I throw a stone in the water.

en stjerne.explanation: "En stjerne" means "a star", either in the sky or as a rating. A hotel with fem stjerner has five stars.

sentence.da: Om natten ser vi en **stjerne** på himlen.
sentence.en: At night we see a star in the sky.

en stol.explanation: "En stol" means "a chair". In Danish you sit på (on) a chair: Sæt dig på stolen (Sit down on the chair).

sentence.da: Jeg sidder på en **stol** ved bordet.
sentence.en: I am sitting on a chair at the table.

en storebror.explanation: "En storebror" means "a big brother": any brother who is older than you, whatever the age gap.

sentence.da: Min **storebror** er ti år ældre end mig.
sentence.en: My big brother is ten years older than me.

en storesøster.explanation: "En storesøster" means "a big sister": any sister who is older than you, whatever the age gap.

sentence.da: Min **storesøster** er tre år ældre end mig.
sentence.en: My big sister is three years older than me.

en storm.explanation: "En storm" means "a storm" with very strong wind. It is stronger than blæst (windy weather) and weaker than en orkan (a hurricane).

sentence.da: Der kommer en **storm** med meget vind.
sentence.en: A storm is coming with a lot of wind.

en strand.explanation: "En strand" means "a beach". På stranden means "at the beach".

sentence.da: Vi ligger i solen på en **strand**.
sentence.en: We lie in the sun on a beach.

sentence.da: Jeg har et hul i min **strømpe**.
sentence.en: I have a hole in my sock.

en stue.explanation: "En stue" means "a living room", the room where you sit, relax and have guests. It also gives the ground floor its name: stueetagen (the ground floor).

sentence.da: Vi har en sofa i vores **stue**.
sentence.en: We have a sofa in our living room.

en størrelse.explanation: "En størrelse" means "a size", for clothes, shoes or anything else. It comes from stor (big), so en større størrelse is a bigger size.

sentence.da: Har I en større **størrelse** i kjolen?
sentence.en: Do you have a bigger size in the dress?

en støvle.explanation: "En støvle" means "a boot". Boots come in pairs, so you often hear et par støvler (a pair of boots). Rubber boots are gummistøvler, built on the same word.

sentence.da: Min venstre **støvle** er våd i regnen.
sentence.en: My left boot is wet in the rain.

en suppe.explanation: "En suppe" means "a soup", as in tomatsuppe (tomato soup). The verb to use is at spise (to eat), not at drikke (to drink).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en varm **suppe** med en ske.
sentence.en: I eat a hot soup with a spoon.

en sweater.explanation: "En sweater" means "a sweater". To say you are wearing one, use have ... på (literally have ... on): Jeg har en sweater på (I am wearing a sweater).

sentence.da: Jeg har en varm **sweater** på i dag.
sentence.en: I am wearing a warm sweater today.

en sygdom.explanation: "En sygdom" means "a disease" or "an illness". It comes from syg (sick). You say Jeg er syg (I am sick) about yourself, and "en sygdom" for the illness itself.

sentence.da: Han er syg og har en alvorlig **sygdom**.
sentence.en: He is sick and has a serious illness.

en sygeplejerske.explanation: "En sygeplejerske" means "a nurse". It comes from sygepleje (nursing). Male nurses are also called "sygeplejerske" in Danish, so the word is not only for women.

sentence.da: Min søster er **sygeplejerske** på et hospital.
sentence.en: My sister is a nurse at a hospital.

en sø.explanation: "En sø" means "a lake", a body of fresh water with land all around it. Do not mix it up with et hav (a sea), which is much bigger and salty.

sentence.da: Der er en lille **sø** i skoven.
sentence.en: There is a small lake in the forest.

en søn.explanation: "En søn" means "a son". It is used for a son of any age, even a grown-up one: Hendes søn er tredive (Her son is thirty).

sentence.en: My son is ten years old.

en søster.explanation: "En søster" means "a sister". For a sister who shares only one parent, say en halvsøster (a half sister).

sentence.da: Min **søster** og jeg har samme mor.
sentence.en: My sister and I have the same mother.

et sekund.explanation: "Et sekund" means "a second". Do not mix it up with second as in number two, which is anden (second). Et øjeblik (a moment) is a similar short wait: Et øjeblik, tak (One moment, please).

sentence.en: It only takes a second.

et skab.explanation: "Et skab" means "a cupboard", and also a cabinet, a closet or a locker: any closed space for storing things. Words are added to say which kind, for example et køleskab (a refrigerator, literally a cooling cupboard).

sentence.en: The plates are in a cupboard.

et skib.explanation: "Et skib" means "a ship". A smaller boat is en båd (a boat), and a cruise ship is et krydstogtskib (a cruise ship).

sentence.da: Et stort **skib** sejler over havet til Norge.
sentence.en: A big ship sails across the sea to Norway.

et skæg.explanation: "Et skæg" means "a beard". En mand med skæg means "a man with a beard". A moustache is et overskæg, literally an over-beard.

sentence.en: My father has a long beard.

et soveværelse.explanation: "Et soveværelse" means "a bedroom". It is built from sove (to sleep) and værelse (room), so it is literally a sleeping room.

sentence.da: Jeg sover i min seng i mit **soveværelse**.
sentence.en: I sleep in my bed in my bedroom.

et spejl.explanation: "Et spejl" means "a mirror". Jeg kigger i spejlet means "I look in the mirror".

sentence.en: I look in a mirror.

et spil.explanation: "Et spil" means "a game", such as a board game, card game or computer game. It comes from at spille (to play), which is also the word for playing music.

sentence.en: Shall we play a game?

et sprog.explanation: "Et sprog" means "a language". Taler du engelsk? means "Do you speak English?".

sentence.en: Which language do you speak?

et spørgsmål.explanation: "Et spørgsmål" means "a question". A polite way to start is Må jeg stille et spørgsmål? (May I ask a question?), which literally says put a question.

sentence.en: The teacher answers my question.

et sted.explanation: "Et sted" means "a place" or "a spot", and also "somewhere": Jeg har set det et sted means "I have seen it somewhere".

sentence.da: Er der et **sted** at spise her?
sentence.en: Is there a place to eat here?

et stoppested.explanation: "Et stoppested" means "a stop". It is built from stoppe (to stop) and sted (place). For a bus, say et busstoppested (a bus stop).

sentence.en: The next stop is the railway station.

et stykke.explanation: "Et stykke" means "a piece", as in et stykke kage (a piece of cake). In shops it also means "each": ti kroner stykket means "ten kroner each".

sentence.en: May I have a piece of cake?

et supermarked.explanation: "Et supermarked" means "a supermarket". It is built from super (super) and marked (market). You can ask Hvor er supermarkedet? (Where is the supermarket?).

sentence.en: I buy milk in a supermarket.

et svar.explanation: "Et svar" means "an answer" or "a reply". Tak for svaret means "thanks for the reply".

sentence.en: Thanks for your answer.

et svin.explanation: "Et svin" means "a pig". Calling a person et svin is rude: Han er et svin means "He is a pig". For the meat, Danes say svinekød (pork).

sentence.en: The farmer has a pig on the farm.

et sygehus.explanation: "Et sygehus" means "a hospital". It is built from syg (sick) and hus (house). Et hospital (a hospital) means the same. Hun er på sygehuset (She is at the hospital).

sentence.da: Lægen og sygeplejerskerne arbejder på et **sygehus**.
sentence.en: The doctor and the nurses work at a hospital.

et sår.explanation: "Et sår" means "a wound" or "a sore", such as a cut or a scrape. Et sår i munden means "a sore in the mouth".

sentence.da: Jeg har et **sår** på mit knæ.
sentence.en: I have a wound on my knee.

salt.explanation: "Salt" means "salt". You do not count it, so you say noget salt (some salt) rather than a salt. The same word also describes taste: det er for salt means "it is too salty".

sentence.da: Jeg vil have lidt **salt** i suppen.
sentence.en: I want a little salt in the soup.

saltet.explanation: "Saltet" means "salted" and comes from at salte (to salt). Do not mix it up with salt, which describes taste and means "salty".

sentence.da: Fisken er **saltet** og smager af salt.
sentence.en: The fish is salted and tastes of salt.

samme.explanation: "Samme" means "same". It usually follows den, det or de (all three mean "the"), but it can also stand alone, as in samme dag (the same day). Det samme is also a reply meaning "the same to you".

sentence.en: We have the same car.

sammen.explanation: "Sammen" means "together". Compare Vi spiser sammen (We eat together) with Jeg spiser alene (I eat alone). Alle sammen means "everyone together", as in Hej alle sammen! (Hello everyone!).

sentence.en: My friend and I live together.

sandaler.explanation: "Sandaler" means "sandals". One sandal is en sandal, but shoes come as a pair, so you mostly hear this more than one form.

sentence.en: I have sandals on today.

seks.explanation: "Seks" means "six". Compare seks børn (six children) with syv børn (seven children). It is used for time too: Klokken er seks (It is six o'clock).

sentence.en: We are six people.

seksten.explanation: "Seksten" means "sixteen". Do not mix it up with seks (six): seks børn (six children), seksten børn (sixteen children). It is used for age: Jeg er seksten år (I am sixteen years old).

sentence.en: Ten plus six is sixteen.

selv.explanation: "Selv" means "myself", yourself, herself and so on, with nobody helping: Jeg gør det selv (I do it myself). At the start of a sentence it means "even": Selv børn kan det (Even children can do it).

sentence.en: I make the food myself.

selv tak.explanation: "Selv tak" means "you're welcome". It literally means "thanks yourself", which is why it also returns thanks: Tak for i aftes - Selv tak (Thanks for last night - Thanks to you too).

forms.en: Thanks for the help. - You're welcome.

forms.da: Tak for i aftes. - Selv tak.
forms.en: Thanks for last night. - Thanks to you too.

sentence.en: "Thanks for the help!" - "You're welcome!"

selvfølgelig.explanation: "Selvfølgelig" means "of course". It agrees to a request, and it also says something is obvious: Hun kommer selvfølgelig for sent (Of course she is coming late).

sentence.en: "May I borrow your book?" - "Of course!"

senere.explanation: "Senere" means "later", as in Vi ses senere (See you later) and senere i dag (later today). Do not mix it up with sent, which means "late": Det er sent (It is late).

sentence.en: I will call you later.

sennep.explanation: "Sennep" means "mustard". You do not count it, so you say noget sennep (some mustard), as in Vil du have noget sennep? (Do you want some mustard?).

sentence.da: Pølsen smager godt med ketchup og **sennep**.
sentence.en: The sausage tastes good with ketchup and mustard.

sent.explanation: "Sent" means "late", as in not early: Vi kom sent hjem (We came home late). Do not mix it up with senere, which means "later". To say you are running late, say Jeg kommer for sent (I am coming too late) or Jeg er forsinket (I am delayed).

sentence.en: We come home late today.

september.explanation: "September" means "September", as in Vi rejser i september (We travel in September).

sentence.en: September is the month after August.

ses i morgen.explanation: "Ses i morgen" means "see you tomorrow". Swap i morgen for another time: ses i aften (see you tonight).

forms.en: Will we see each other tomorrow?

sentence.da: Jeg skal hjem nu. **Ses i morgen**!
sentence.en: I am going home now. See you tomorrow!

shampoo.explanation: "Shampoo" means "shampoo" and is spelled the same as in English. You do not count it, so you say noget shampoo (some shampoo).

sentence.en: I wash my hair with shampoo.

shorts.explanation: "Shorts" means "shorts". It is always used for more than one: Mine shorts er nye (My shorts are new).

sentence.en: I am wearing shorts and a T-shirt.

siden.explanation: "Siden" means "since" and also "ago". Since: siden i går (since yesterday). Ago: for to år siden (two years ago), where siden comes last.

sentence.en: I have lived here since 2020.

sidst.explanation: "Sidst" means "last" in the sense of coming after everyone else or at the end: Jeg kom sidst (I came last). Before a thing, use sidste, as in sidste gang (the last time).

sentence.en: He came last to the party.

sidste.explanation: "Sidste" means "last" before a thing: den sidste bus (the last bus), sidste uge (last week), sidste år (last year). Compare Jeg kom sidst (I came last), where sidst stands alone with nothing after it.

sentence.da: Det er den **sidste** bus i dag.
sentence.en: It is the last bus today.

sig.explanation: "Sig" means "himself", herself, itself or "themselves". Compare Han vasker ham (He washes him — someone else) with Han vasker sig (He washes himself). For "I" and "we" use mig (myself) and os (ourselves): Jeg vasker mig (I wash myself). Some verbs always come with sig even though English has no word for it: at skynde sig (to hurry), at glæde sig (to look forward to).

forms.en: She is looking forward to it.

sentence.en: He washes himself every morning.

sikker.explanation: "Sikker" means "sure" and "safe": Er du sikker? (Are you sure?), Jeg er sikker (I am sure), en sikker bil (a safe car).

sentence.en: I am completely sure about it.

sin.explanation: "Sin" means "his own", her own or "its own" before an en-word. Compare Peter ser sin bror (Peter sees his own brother) with Peter ser Jens og hans bror (Peter sees Jens and Jens's brother). For "I" and "you" use min (my) and din (your): Jeg ser min bror (I see my brother).

sentence.en: She loves her (own) dog.

sine.explanation: "Sine" means "his own" or "her own" for more than one thing. Compare Peter ser sine venner (Peter sees his own friends) with Peter ser Jens og hans venner (Peter sees Jens and Jens's friends). For one thing use sin (en-word) or sit (et-word): sin bror (his own brother).

sentence.en: She calls her (own) parents.

sit.explanation: "Sit" means "his own", her own or "its own" before an et-word. Compare Peter elsker sit hus (Peter loves his own house) with Peter ser Jens og hans hus (Peter sees Jens and Jens's house). For an en-word use sin: sin bil (his own car).

sentence.en: He looks after his (own) child.

sjette.explanation: "Sjette" means "sixth", as in det sjette æg (the sixth egg). It is used for dates too: den sjette maj (the sixth of May). It is not spelled sekste, even though seks (six) is the number it comes from.

sentence.en: After the fifth floor comes the sixth floor.

sjov.explanation: "Sjov" means "fun" and also "funny": a party and a joke can both be sjov. Det var sjovt means "That was fun", and "for sjov" means "for fun" or "as a joke".

sentence.en: The film is very funny.

skandinavien.explanation: "Skandinavien" means "Scandinavia". Place names start with a capital letter in Danish, but skandinavisk (Scandinavian) does not. To include Finland and Iceland too, Danes say Norden (the Nordic countries).

sentence.en: Denmark is in Scandinavia.

sko.explanation: "Sko" means "shoes". It looks the same for one shoe and many: en sko (one shoe), mine sko (my shoes). Danish often says the where English says my: Jeg tager skoene på (I put my shoes on).

sentence.da: Jeg tager **sko** på og går ud.
sentence.en: I put shoes on and go out.

skyet.explanation: "Skyet" means "cloudy". It comes from en sky (a cloud). In weather forecasts you also hear overskyet (overcast), when clouds cover the whole sky.

sentence.da: I dag er det **skyet** og koldt.
sentence.en: Today it is cloudy and cold.

skynd dig.explanation: "Skynd dig" means "hurry up" and is said to one person. To several people, say skynd jer. The little words dig and "jer" mean yourself (one person) and yourselves (several people).

forms.da: Skynd dig, vi er sent på den.

sentence.en: Hurry up, the train leaves now!

skål.explanation: "Skål" means "cheers". Add for and a name or dig (you) to toast someone: Skål for dig! (Cheers to you!). It is the same word as en skål (a bowl).

sentence.en: We raise the glasses and say cheers!

slidt.explanation: "Slidt" means "worn": old and used up from much use, as in en slidt sofa (a worn sofa). It is also used about people: Jeg er helt slidt means "I am completely worn out".

sentence.en: The sofa is old and very worn.

slik.explanation: "Slik" means candy (sweets). You do not count it and normally use it without a: Jeg spiser for meget slik (I eat too much candy).

sentence.en: Children love candy and cake.

slut.explanation: "Slut" means "over" or "finished", used after er (is): Ferien er slut (The holiday is over). It also means something has run out: Mælken er slut (The milk has run out).

sentence.en: The school day is over now.

smal.explanation: "Smal" means "narrow", for streets, paths, doors and windows. It is about width, not about being thin like paper; for that use tynd (thin).

sentence.en: The little street is very narrow.

smuk.explanation: "Smuk" means "beautiful", for people, places, views and things. It is a bit stronger than pæn (nice-looking). Hvor er det smukt! means "How beautiful it is!"

sentence.en: She is wearing a beautiful dress.

smør.explanation: "Smør" means "butter". The word for spreading it is at smøre (to spread), which looks almost the same. Smørrebrød is literally butter-bread, a slice of bread with toppings.

sentence.da: Vil du have **smør** på dit brød?
sentence.en: Do you want butter on your bread?

snart.explanation: "Snart" means "soon": Vi ses snart (See you soon). With a clock time it means "almost": Klokken er snart ti (It is almost ten o'clock). Så snart means "as soon as".

sentence.en: The food will be ready soon.

snavset.explanation: "Snavset" means "dirty", as in en snavset skjorte (a dirty shirt). It comes from snavs (dirt).

sentence.en: My shirt is very dirty.

sne.explanation: "Sne" means "snow". To say that it is snowing, use Det sner (It is snowing). It is also part of words like en snemand (a snowman) and en snebold (a snowball).

sentence.en: The children make a snowman out of snow.

sokker.explanation: "Sokker" means "socks". Danish often joins two words into one, so wool socks are uldsokker, from uld (wool) and "sokker".

sentence.en: I put on socks and shoes.

solbriller.explanation: "Solbriller" means "sunglasses", from sol (sun) and briller (glasses). It is always used for more than one, even for a single pair. Briller on its own means glasses you see with.

sentence.en: I put on sunglasses in the sun.

solcreme.explanation: "Solcreme" means "sunscreen", from sol (sun) and creme (cream). When you talk about it in general, you leave out a: Husk solcreme! (Remember sunscreen!).

sentence.da: Husk at tage **solcreme** med på stranden.
sentence.en: Remember to bring sunscreen to the beach.

solrig.explanation: "Solrig" means "sunny". When you just say how the weather is, use solrigt: Det er solrigt i dag (It is sunny today).

sentence.da: Det er en varm og **solrig** dag.
sentence.en: It is a warm and sunny day.

solrigt.explanation: "Solrigt" means "sunny". You use it with vejr (weather): solrigt vejr (sunny weather), and after det er: Det er solrigt (It is sunny).

sentence.da: I dag er det **solrigt** og varmt.
sentence.en: Today it is sunny and warm.

solskin.explanation: "Solskin" means "sunshine", made of sol (sun) and skin (shine). The verb is at skinne (to shine): Solen skinner (The sun is shining).

sentence.en: We enjoy sunshine in the garden.

solskinsvejr.explanation: "Solskinsvejr" means "sunny weather", from solskin (sunshine) and vejr (weather). Example: Hvis det er solskinsvejr, tager vi på stranden (If it is sunny, we go to the beach).

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at gå tur i **solskinsvejr**.
sentence.en: It is lovely to go for a walk in sunny weather.

som.explanation: "Som" means "who", that or "which" when it joins two parts of a sentence: manden, som bor her (the man who lives here), bogen, som jeg læser (the book that I read). It also means "like" or "as": Han er som sin far (He is like his father), Jeg arbejder som lærer (I work as a teacher).

sentence.da: Det er den bog, **som** jeg læser.
sentence.en: That is the book that I am reading.

somme tider.explanation: "Somme tider" means "sometimes", for things that happen now and then, not every day: Somme tider tager jeg bussen (Sometimes I take the bus).

sentence.da: Jeg er **somme tider** træt om morgenen.
sentence.en: I am sometimes tired in the morning.

sommetider.explanation: "Sommetider" means "sometimes", for things that happen now and then, not every day: Sommetider spiser vi ude (Sometimes we eat out).

forms.en: I sometimes go for a walk

sentence.en: Sometimes I take the bike to work.

sort.explanation: "Sort" means "black", as in en sort bil (a black car). It is also used in sort kaffe (black coffee).

sentence.en: The night is dark and black.

sov godt.explanation: "Sov godt" means "sleep well". Sov comes from at sove (to sleep) and godt means "well".

sentence.en: Good night, sleep well!

spaghetti.explanation: "Spaghetti" means "spaghetti", spelled the same as in English. You do not count it: en tallerken spaghetti (a plate of spaghetti).

sentence.en: We eat spaghetti with meat sauce.

spanien.explanation: "Spanien" means "Spain". Example: Jeg elsker Spanien (I love Spain). Countries take i for being there and til for going there, as in the forms above.

sentence.en: We are on holiday in Spain.

spansk.explanation: "Spansk" means "Spanish", for things from Spain and for the language. Danish writes it with a small letter. For the language: Jeg taler spansk (I speak Spanish).

sentence.en: In Spain people speak Spanish.

spinat.explanation: "Spinat" means "spinach". For spinach in general you leave out en: Jeg elsker spinat (I love spinach). Rå spinat means "raw spinach".

sentence.en: I boil green spinach for dinner.

sport.explanation: "Sport" means "sport", and for sport in general you leave out en. At dyrke sport means "to do sport": Han dyrker meget sport (He does a lot of sport).

sentence.en: Football and tennis are sport.

spændende.explanation: "Spændende" means "exciting" or "interesting". Det lyder spændende means "That sounds exciting". Interessant (interesting) is milder and fits less thrilling things.

sentence.en: I am reading an exciting book.

stadig.explanation: "Stadig" means "still", for something that is continuing: Jeg er stadig træt (I am still tired). Endnu (yet) is used for something that has not happened: ikke endnu means "not yet".

sentence.en: The child is still sleeping at ten o'clock.

stadigvæk.explanation: "Stadigvæk" means "still", for something that keeps going: Det regner stadigvæk (It is still raining). It means the same as stadig (still). Endnu (yet) is different: ikke endnu means "not yet".

sentence.en: He still lives with his mother.

stegt.explanation: "Stegt" means "fried" or "roasted", depending on the food: stegt flæsk (fried pork) and stegt kylling (roast chicken).

sentence.en: I want fried fish.

stille.explanation: "Stille" means "quiet", silent or "calm": Vær stille means "Be quiet". For a calm, relaxed person rolig (calm) also fits. Do not mix it up with at stille (to put or place), as in at stille et spørgsmål (to ask a question).

sentence.en: It is very quiet in the house.

stop.explanation: "Stop" means "stop". Adding lige (just) makes it softer: Stop lige! (Hold on a second!).

sentence.en: Stop! A car is coming!

stor.explanation: "Stor" means "big" or "large". It can also mean "grown-up": Hvor er du blevet stor! means "How big you have grown!"

sentence.en: The elephant is very big.

storbritannien.explanation: "Storbritannien" means "Great Britain". It is built from stor (big) and Britannien (Britain). Example: Vi rejser til Storbritannien (We travel to Great Britain).

sentence.en: London is in Great Britain.

stærk.explanation: "Stærk" means "strong", for people, coffee, tea, wind and feelings: stærk kaffe is strong coffee. For food it also means "hot" or "spicy".

sentence.en: I drink strong coffee every morning.

størst.explanation: "Størst" means "biggest" or "largest". Compare Hun er større (She is bigger) with Han er størst (He is the biggest).

sentence.en: The elephant is the biggest of the animals.

støvler.explanation: "Støvler" means "boots". A pair is et par støvler (a pair of boots).

sentence.en: I put on boots in the rain.

sukker.explanation: "Sukker" means "sugar". You can ask for a little in your drink: lidt sukker i kaffen (a little sugar in the coffee).

sentence.en: I want sugar in my coffee.

sulten.explanation: "Sulten" means "hungry". You say Jeg er sulten (I am hungry). To ask, say Er du sulten? (Are you hungry?).

sentence.da: Jeg er meget **sulten** og vil spise.
sentence.en: I am very hungry and want to eat.

sund.explanation: "Sund" means "healthy", good for your body: sund mad (healthy food). Do not mix it up with rask (well, not sick): Jeg er rask igen (I am well again).

sentence.en: Apples and carrots are healthy food.

sundhed.explanation: "Sundhed" means "health" in a general sense, such as how healthy a lifestyle or a country is. For a person's own condition Danes usually say helbred (health): Han har dårligt helbred (He is in poor health).

forms.en: It is good for your health.

sentence.da: Frugt og søvn er gode for din **sundhed**.
sentence.en: Fruit and sleep are good for your health.

super.explanation: "Super" means "great". It can stand alone: Super! (Great!). Before another word it makes it stronger: super god (really good).

sentence.da: Vi har en **super** dag i parken.
sentence.en: We have a great day in the park.

svensk.explanation: "Svensk" means "Swedish". It is also the name of the language: Jeg taler svensk (I speak Swedish).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Sverige og er **svensk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Sweden and is Swedish.

sverige.explanation: "Sverige" means "Sweden". Do not mix it up with Schweiz (Switzerland), which is a different country.

sentence.da: **Sverige** er et land ved siden af Danmark.
sentence.en: Sweden is a country next to Denmark.

svimmel.explanation: "Svimmel" means "dizzy", the feeling that the room is spinning. You say Jeg er svimmel (I am dizzy) or Jeg bliver svimmel (I am getting dizzy).

sentence.da: Jeg er **svimmel** og skal sidde ned.
sentence.en: I am dizzy and need to sit down.

svinekød.explanation: "Svinekød" means "pork". It is built from svin (pig) and kød (meat), so it is literally pig meat.

sentence.en: Pork is meat from a pig.

svær.explanation: "Svær" means "difficult" or "hard to do". Det er svært means "It is hard", and "Det er svært at lære dansk" means "It is hard to learn Danish".

sentence.en: The task is very difficult for me.

svømning.explanation: "Svømning" means "swimming" as an activity or class. Compare Jeg kan svømme (I can swim) with Jeg har svømning (I have a swimming class).

sentence.da: Børnene har **svømning** i svømmehallen i dag.
sentence.en: The children have swimming in the swimming pool today.

syd.explanation: "Syd" means "south". Compare Det er varmt i syd (It is warm in the south) with Det er koldt i nord (It is cold in the north). Use mod syd for the direction: Vi kører mod syd (We drive south).

sentence.en: The birds fly south in the winter.

sydamerika.explanation: "Sydamerika" means "South America". It is made from syd (south) and Amerika (America).

sentence.en: Brazil and Argentina are in South America.

syg.explanation: "Syg" means "sick" or "ill": Jeg er syg (I am sick). At melde sig syg means "to call in sick".

sentence.da: Min søn er **syg** og bliver hjemme.
sentence.en: My son is sick and stays home.

syltetøj.explanation: "Syltetøj" means "jam". Put a fruit in front to name the kind: hindbærsyltetøj (raspberry jam), blommesyltetøj (plum jam).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have **syltetøj** på mit brød.
sentence.en: I want jam on my bread.

sytten.explanation: "Sytten" means "seventeen". Do not mix it up with syv (seven): syv børn (seven children), sytten børn (seventeen children). Example: Jeg er sytten år (I am seventeen years old).

sentence.en: After sixteen comes seventeen.

syv.explanation: "Syv" means "seven". Do not mix it up with sytten (seventeen): syv dage (seven days) but sytten dage (seventeen days).

sentence.da: Der er **syv** dage i en uge.
sentence.en: There are seven days in a week.

syvende.explanation: "Syvende" means "seventh". Compare syv æg (seven eggs) with det syvende æg (the seventh egg). It is used for dates too: den syvende juli (the seventh of July).

sentence.da: Søndag er den **syvende** dag i ugen.
sentence.en: Sunday is the seventh day of the week.

så.explanation: "Så" means "so" or "then". Compare Det regner, så vi bliver hjemme (It is raining, so we stay home) with Først spiser vi, og så går vi (First we eat, and then we go). Before a describing word it adds strength: så stor (so big). Careful: så is also the past of at se (to see): Jeg så ham (I saw him).

sentence.en: I am so happy today!

så længe.explanation: "Så længe" means "as long as". It is different from indtil (until): Jeg bliver, indtil du kommer (I stay until you come). On its own it means "for now": Vent her så længe (Wait here for now).

forms.en: Stay as long as you like

sentence.en: Stay as long as you want.

sådan.explanation: "Sådan" means "like that" or "this way". Compare Gør det sådan (Do it like this) with sådan en bil (a car like that). Said on its own, Sådan! means "There you go!" or "That's it!".

sentence.en: Look, I do it like this.

sæbe.explanation: "Sæbe" means "soap". For an amount you say noget sæbe (some soap) or et stykke sæbe (a piece of soap). Dish soap is a different word: opvaskemiddel (washing-up liquid).

sentence.da: Jeg vasker mine hænder med **sæbe** og vand.
sentence.en: I wash my hands with soap and water.

sød.explanation: "Sød" means "sweet" in taste (sød kage, sweet cake) and also "sweet" or "cute" for people, animals and small children. A common phrase is Det er sødt af dig (That is sweet of you).

sentence.en: The cake is too sweet for me.

sølv.explanation: "Sølv" means "silver", both the metal and the colour. In sport it is also the second-place medal: Hun vandt sølv (She won silver).

sentence.en: My ring is made of silver.

søndag.explanation: "Søndag" means "Sunday". Day names are written with a small letter in Danish. Say på søndag (on Sunday) for this coming Sunday and om søndagen (on Sundays) for every Sunday.

sentence.en: After Saturday comes Sunday.
